Apple Kicks off WWDC 2026 ---------------------------- Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL ) launches its 2026 Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) in Cupertino today, with a new AI strategy widely anticipated.

A keynote later today should showcase a new version of its Siri digital assistant at the core of its AI world, plus a revamp of operating system software across the board – iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27.

* “Developers will be able to more easily integrate AI into their apps using a new system called CoreAI”: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman noted planned advances in services available for AI agent developers, with the new software expected to reach consumers in the fall.

items.title: Item 27
items.text: * “Developers will be able to more easily integrate AI into their apps using a new system called CoreAI”: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman noted planned advances in services available for AI agent developers, with the new software expected to reach consumers in the fall. * “From the department of Really?”: Fool analyst Seth Jayson had earlier this year expressed skepticism about Apple’s new Siri, as reports suggested it will have “a feature set no different than what OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and others have been offering for years.” Revisit the outlook for Apple at Q2 time -----------------------------

links.title: Revisit the outlook for Apple at Q2 time

items.title: Item 2
items.text: Markets End Winning Streak ----------------------------- A move away from tech stocks saw the Nasdaq fall 4.7% last week, with the S&P 500 losing 2.6% to end a nine-week winning streak – though futures turned positive this morning, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq up 0.2% and 0.7% respectively. Chip stocks led the losses, with Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO ) falling over 12% the day after its Q2 earnings update disappointed on guidance – while Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang warned of a lengthy global chip shortage. * “Whatever happened to the stock market, you should be very happy because now you can buy at a discount”: Huang – in Seoul agreeing a contract with SK Hynix – said “Everybody should be very excited,” even as South Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 9% to trigger a trading halt. * Key inflation measures this week: Wednesday’s May consumer price index (CPI) is expected to show a jump to 4.2% year over year – but with core CPI softer at 2.9%. May’s producer price index (PPI) is due Thursday. Check May's strong jobs report ------------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 3
items.text:
Key Earnings This Week from Team RB Recommendations ------------------------------------------------------ * Vail Resorts (NYSE:MTN ) – also a Dividend Investor rec – reports its third quarter after today’s closing bell, after a difficult Q2 saw extreme weather impact guest numbers at leading U.S. ski destinations. Management guided to net income in fiscal 2026 of $144 to $190 million. * Chewy (NYSE:CHWY ) delivers a Q1 update Wednesday, and investors should watch for subscriptions and customer growth translating into higher GAAP profitability and expanded margins. * Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE ) posts Q2 results Thursday, as the company negotiates the challenge to traditional software development from the new AI generation. * Casey's General Stores (NASDAQ:CASY ) – beating the S&P 500 by 12.9% since its latest Stock Advisor recommendation – will report Q4 and full-year fiscal 2026 Tuesday, following strong growth in Q3 . items.title: Item 4
items.text: More Notable Earnings to Watch: ASO, OXM, ORCL ------------------------------------------------- * Academy Sports and Outdoors (NASDAQ:ASO ) – recommended in Dividend Investor – starts its new fiscal year with a 2026 Q1 update Tuesday, after lifting its dividend 15% in Q4. * Oxford Industries (NYSE:OXM ), also a DI rec, reports Q1 Wednesday. Management expects the full year to be stable, or up slightly. * Oracle (NYSE:ORCL ) closes fiscal 2026 with Q4 earnings Wednesday, the first under new CFO Hilary Maxson – tasked with overseeing finances for the company’s big push into AI and cloud growth. Read Tim Beyers on ORCL's "RPO Nonsense" ---------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 5
items.text: 3 Billion People. One Company Nobody Talks About --------------------------------------------------- You have to go down to the late 1800s the agricultural revolution, and 70, 80% of people were working on farms, and then suddenly, machinery came in and 40% of people had to find jobs somewhere else. We're at that type of inflection that is material. —ANTHONY GOONETILLEKE, HEAD OF STRATEGY, AMDOCS Anthony Goonetilleke Watch the video/read the transcript ******************************************

items.text: Today’s Take: The Story vs. the Numbers ****************************************** JP Bennett The holy grail of investing is finding businesses where the numbers end up making the narrative look conservative. — JP BENNETT • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to reveal how you balance a stock's story versus its numbers, or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! items.title: Item 7
items.text: Your Take ************** FRIDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked, how comfortable are you investing in companies based on future margin improvement that's 'mostly theoretical'? J Member jenesuispasdave said “Not comfortable at all. After getting burned a number of times I'm learning to wait for confirmation before investing in a thesis. I need some evidence, even though that can mean missing out on larger gains if the thesis proves true.” See more great answers from our Foolish community TODAY’S QUESTION The Nasdaq fell 4.2% on Friday alone, as investors rotated out of AI and semiconductor stocks. Did that feel like a healthy breather the market needed, or the start of something more concerning? What's your read? Share in the comments on today’s article!
